## Caption (verbatim)

```
Every saint was once exactly where you are. 🤍

Broken. Doubting. Wondering if God had forgotten them.

Augustine spent years chasing the wrong things — pleasure, fame, approval. He ran from God so far he thought he'd never find his way back. And then one day, sitting in a garden in Milan, weeping over his wasted years, he heard a child's voice say: "Take and read." He opened Scripture. And everything changed.

Thérèse of Lisieux never led an army. Never performed a dramatic miracle. She entered the convent at 15 and died at 24 of tuberculosis — unknown, hidden, forgotten by the world. But she discovered something the world still can't understand: that the smallest act of love, done with great faith, moves the heart of God more than any grand gesture.

Francis had everything — wealth, status, a future handed to him. He gave it all away. Every single thing. And in that emptiness, he found a fullness the rest of us spend our whole lives searching for.

And Joan — just a teenage girl from a farming village — stood before kings and generals and said, "God sent me." They laughed. She didn't flinch. She rode into battle not because she wasn't afraid, but because her trust in God was bigger than her fear.

These saints aren't distant statues behind glass. They were real people with real struggles. And every single one of them has something to say to you — right now, in the middle of whatever you're going through.

The question isn't whether God has a saint walking with you.

The question is: are you ready to listen?

ALWAYS REMEMBER:
"Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us."
— Hebrews 12:1
```
